correctness.rationale: For any ordered distinct x,y, the positive/negative barycentric difference has nonzero normalization and disjoint supports; its straight-line interpolation is an explicit continuous G- and particle-swap-equivariant strong deformation retraction onto the cubical deleted product. The quotient of its barycentric subdivision is an honest Delta-complex because each flag contains distinct cell dimensions. Exhaustive standard-library reconstruction yields cubical cells (28,72,42), subdivided cells (142,480,336), orbit cells (8,15,8), and verifies eight uniquely free triangle/edge pairs followed by seven uniquely free edge/vertex pairs to one vertex. This proves X/G contractible, not just a numerical homology claim.

value.rationale: The full cube graph symmetry quotient is a canonical collision-free two-particle moduli space, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The quotient is contractible even though the unreduced two-particle space has Euler characteristic -2. Giving a small explicit collapsible orbit model advances the topological symmetry-reduction question beyond the known general finite configuration models or field-homology invariants; the result is self-contained and reproducible.
